subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: If A and B are independent, then A' and B are:
questions.explain: If A and B are independent, so are A' and B.

questions.q: A box has 4 good and 1 faulty fuse. Two are drawn without replacement. P(both good)?
On a tree diagram, the probabilities on the branches leaving a single node must:
questions.explain: The branches from one node cover all outcomes, so their probabilities sum to 1.

questions.q: P(A | B) = 0.6 and P(B) = 0.5. Find P(A intersect B).
questions.explain: P(A intersect B) = P(A | B)P(B) = 0.6 x 0.5 = 0.3.

questions.q: Two events have P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A intersect B) = 0.2. Are they independent?
options: Yes, since they are mutually exclusive
questions.explain: P(A)P(B) = 0.5 x 0.4 = 0.2 = P(A intersect B), so they are independent.

questions.q: If A and B are mutually exclusive, then P(A intersect B) equals:
questions.explain: Mutually exclusive events cannot occur together, so P(A intersect B) = 0.

questions.q: A fair die is rolled. What is P(rolling a prime number)?
questions.explain: Primes on a die are 2, 3 and 5, giving 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.q: If P(A | B) = P(A), then A and B are:
questions.explain: P(A | B) = P(A) is the definition of A being independent of B.

questions.q: For events with P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.5 and P(A intersect B) = 0.2, find P(A union B).
P(A) = 0.45, P(B) = 0.55 and P(A intersect B) = 0.25. Find P(A only), i.e. A but not B.
questions.explain: P(A intersect B') = P(A) - P(A intersect B) = 0.45 - 0.25 = 0.20.

questions.q: With P(A) = 0.6, P(B | A) = 0.5 and P(B | A') = 0.25, find P(B).
P(A) = 0.7, P(B) = 0.6 and P(A union B) = 0.9. Find P(A intersect B).
questions.explain: Rearranging the addition rule: P(A intersect B) = 0.7 + 0.6 - 0.9 = 0.4.

questions.q: In P(A union B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A intersect B), subtracting P(A intersect B) corrects for:
questions.explain: Subtracting P(A intersect B) removes the overlap otherwise counted in both P(A) and P(B).

questions.q: A spinner lands on 1, 2, 3, 4 with probabilities 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4. P(an even number)?
questions.explain: Even outcomes are 2 and 4: 0.2 + 0.4 = 0.6.

questions.q: A bag has 3 red and 5 blue balls. Two are drawn without replacement. P(both red)?
Two events have P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A intersect B) = 0.3. Are they independent?
options: No, since 0.5 x 0.4 = 0.2 which is not 0.3
questions.explain: P(A)P(B) = 0.2 does not equal P(A intersect B) = 0.3, so they are not independent.

questions.q: P(A) = 0.5 and P(B) = 0.3 are mutually exclusive. Find P((A union B)').
questions.explain: P(A union B) = 0.8, so the complement is 1 - 0.8 = 0.2.

questions.q: P(A intersect B) = 0.2 and P(A) = 0.5. Find P(B | A).
questions.explain: P(B | A) = P(A intersect B)/P(A) = 0.2/0.5 = 0.4.

questions.q: Given P(A intersect B) = 0.12 and P(B) = 0.3, find P(A | B).
questions.explain: P(A | B) = P(A intersect B)/P(B) = 0.12/0.3 = 0.4.

questions.q: A coin is tossed and a fair die rolled. P(head and a six)?
questions.explain: Independent events: (1/2) x (1/6) = 1/12.

questions.q: Two cards are drawn with replacement from a standard 52-card deck. P(both hearts)?
In a Venn diagram, the region representing A but not B is:
questions.explain: A and not B is the intersection of A with the complement of B, written A intersect B'.

questions.q: A and B are independent with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.5. What is P(A intersect B)?
questions.explain: For independent events P(A intersect B) = P(A)P(B) = 0.4 x 0.5 = 0.2.

questions.q: Two independent events each have probability 0.8. P(at least one occurs)?
questions.explain: P(at least one) = 1 - P(neither) = 1 - 0.2 x 0.2 = 1 - 0.04 = 0.96.

questions.q: P(rain) = 0.3. If it rains P(late) = 0.6; if not, P(late) = 0.2. Find P(late).
P(A') = 0.35. What is P(A)?
Among 40 students, 25 study Maths, 18 study Physics and 10 study both. How many study neither?
questions.explain: At least one = 25 + 18 - 10 = 33, so neither = 40 - 33 = 7.

questions.q: Among the same 40 students (25 Maths, 18 Physics, 10 both), P(a random student studies Maths only)?
questions.explain: Maths only = 25 - 10 = 15, so the probability = 15/40.

questions.q: Events A and B are mutually exclusive with P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.45. What is P(A union B)?
questions.explain: For mutually exclusive events P(A union B) = P(A) + P(B) = 0.3 + 0.45 = 0.75.

questions.q: For independent A and B with P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.5, find P(A union B).
questions.explain: P(A intersect B) = 0.15, so P(A union B) = 0.3 + 0.5 - 0.15 = 0.65.
